decisive_items: right temporal lobe ring-enhancing lesion measuring 5.7 cm × 4.8 cm × 5.2 cm with a gas-fluid level and gas bubbles
Cultures revealed Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus gallinarum
Medical history included right tympanomastoidectomy for cholesteatoma 2 months prior
response.rationale: Ring-enhancing temporal lobe lesion with gas and otogenic source (recent mastoidectomy, mastoid discharge) plus cultured organisms strongly indicate otogenic brain abscess; R7 is broader and lacks the otogenic link.

rejected.why: Cholesteatoma is historical context, not the acute intracranial lesion.
Cerebral infection is too nonspecific; imaging and microbiology specify abscess.
Subdural empyema is not supported; lesion is intraparenchymal ring-enhancing.
Post-surgical infection is generic and does not capture the brain abscess.
Mastoiditis alone does not explain the temporal lobe ring-enhancing lesion.
Otitic hydrocephalus lacks evidence of hydrocephalus and does not match imaging.
